previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with bipolar disorder, asthma, and a history of multiple suicide attempts was admitted after being found unresponsive in her car following a drug overdose involving clonidine, haloperidol, and olanzapine. She presented with a GCS of 8, bradycardia, and respiratory depression requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. Initial labs showed an elevated lactate and anion gap metabolic acidosis, both of which resolved with fluid resuscitation. CT head showed no acute intracranial abnormalities. She developed a prolonged QT interval, likely due to the overdose and bradycardia, which improved with supportive care and electrolyte repletion. She was extubated without complications and regained full mental clarity. Phlebitis at an IV site was noted but remained mild. Psychiatry recommended continuation of lithium therapy. She was medically stabilized and transferred to a psychiatric facility for ongoing care.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ was admitted to the gynecology service on ___ 
for the work-up of her left lower quadrant pain. The patient has 
a history of chronic pelvic pain thought to be secondary to 
endometriosis, and was also pregnant at 15w2d on the day of 
admission. 

The patient was admitted for observation, and for pain control. 
A Pelvic ultrasound did not reveal any ovarian torsion and a MRI 
was within normal limits without clear explanation of her LLQ 
pain. The patient initially had nausea, which was thought to be 
secondary to N/V of pregnancy. On the day of admission, with 
anti-emetics, the patient was able to tolerate a regular diet 
without N/V. Her pain remained stable throughout her hospital 
course, and given that there was no identifiable cause of her 
LLQ other than possibly her endometriosis, the team felt that it 
was safe for outpatient monitoring.

On the day of discharge, the patient was tolerating a regular 
diet, voiding spontaneously, ambulating and had reassuring fetal 
heart checks everyday. She was discharged with follow-up at the 
pain clniic and with her primary OB.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  PELVIS, NON-OBSTETRIC

INDICATION:  Evaluate for torsion or cyst in a patient with acute onset left
lower quadrant pain, 15 weeks pregnant.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale ultrasound images of the pelvis were obtained with
transabdominal approach followed by transvaginal approach for further
delineation of uterine and ovarian anatomy.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

A single live fetus is seen within the uterus.  The bilateral ovaries are
normal in size and demonstrate normal waveforms.  There is no free fluid.

IMPRESSION:


1. No evidence of ovarian torsion.
2. Single live fetus seen within the uterus.

EXAMINATION:  MRI abdomen and pelvis without contrast.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with LLQ pain of unclear etiology. No clinical
evidence of bowel obstruction, torsion. Currently 15 weeks pregnant  // source
of LLQ pain

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1 and T2 weighted sequences were obtained in a 1.5
Tesla magnet without administration of intravenous contrast.

COMPARISON:  Ultrasound from ___.

FINDINGS: 

The lung bases are grossly clear.  There is no pleural or pericardial
effusion.
The liver is normal in size and signal, without gross focal lesions.  The
gallbladder is normal.  The intra and extrahepatic biliary ducts are normal in
caliber.  The pancreas is normal in size and signal, without focal masses or
ductal dilatation.  The spleen is normal in size.
Mild bilateral hydronephrosis is present, more on the right, physiologic for
pregnancy.  The adrenals are normal.
The bowel is unremarkable.
Single intrauterine pregnancy is demonstrated, with anterior placenta.  This
examination is not intended to evaluate the fetus.
Both ovaries are well seen and are normal (7:66).
There is no free fluid in the abdomen and pelvis.
There is no retroperitoneal, mesenteric or pelvic lymphadenopathy.
The bone marrow signal is normal.

IMPRESSION:


1. Normal examination.  No finding to explain left lower quadrant pain.
2. Single intrauterine pregnancy with anterior placenta.
